newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish police name British bomb targets.
newsitem.headline: Danish police name British bomb targets.

text.p: Danish police said on Monday letter bombs posted by suspected neo-Nazis to London were addressed to television presenter Sharron Davies, an anti-fascist organisation and the neo-Nazi group Combat 18, to which the Danish suspects themselves are believed linked.

"One theory is that there is an internal power struggle within the Combat 18 organisation, we know that there has been internal fighting in Nazi circles," Copenhagen murder squad chief Kurt Jensen told the Danish news agency Ritzau.

"Another possibility is that they were trying to disguise the identity of the sender. Combat 18 in London could have been warned in advance and it would have appeared as someone else was behind the letter bombs," Jensen said.

Danish detectives arrested a group of seven suspected local neo-Nazis at the weekend after police seized three letter bombs -- explosive devices hidden in video cassettes -- posted in Sweden to addresses in London.
British newspapers said that among those targetted were Davies, former heavyweight boxing champion Frank Bruno and England international footballer Paul Ince.
Bruno and Ince are black, both married to whites. Davies, a former Olympic swimmer, is white and married to black athlete Derek Redmond.
